title: Valid Binary Strings With Cost Limit
summary: Given integers n and k, find all binary strings of length n that do not have two consecutive '1's and whose indices sum to a cost no greater than k.
statement: Given integers n and k, find all binary strings of length n that do not have two consecutive '1's and whose indices sum to a cost no greater than k. Return these strings in any order.
constraints: n is positive and k is nonnegative.
A valid length-n binary string has no adjacent ones.
Its cost is the sum of zero-based indices containing one; return every valid string with cost at most k in lexicographic order.
hints: Build the answer left to right so adjacent and cost constraints are local.
Always branch to zero; branch to one only after zero and within remaining cost.
At index i recurse with unchanged cost for zero or cost+i for allowed one.
Every accepted string has one unique decision path, and zero-first traversal gives lexicographic order.
editorial: Every accepted string has one unique decision path, and zero-first traversal gives lexicographic order.

tests.explanation: The valid strings within cost one are 000, 010, and 100.
Strings 00 and 10 have cost zero and no adjacent ones.
